PullRequest.Title: Never send Entra sign-in tokens to the marketplace
PullRequest.Body:
<!-- Thank you for submitting a Pull Request. Please:
* Read our Pull Request guidelines:
  https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/wiki/How-to-Contribute#pull-requests
* Associate an issue with the Pull Request.
* Ensure that the code is up-to-date with the `main` branch.

Related to [microsoft/vscode#325412](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/issues/325412). Focused follow-up to [microsoft/vscode#325804](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/pull/325804).

## Change

Remove the Microsoft marketplace provider's fallback to the sign-in access token when protected resource metadata or a resource-scoped session is unavailable. The sign-in credential remains a local eligibility signal, not a marketplace bearer.

Also skip silent resource-session lookup and interactive resource consent when metadata advertises no scopes, instead of substituting the sign-in scopes.

Open marketplaces continue anonymously. Gated marketplaces continue to require sign-in or consent when a resource token cannot be acquired. Account selection, tenant eligibility, and consent for advertised resource scopes are preserved. This PR does not change renewal, metadata caching, or HTTP status mapping.

## Regression coverage

The marketplace manifest suite inspects actual outgoing Authorization headers and complete manifest IPC arguments for both the shared process and remote server. Cases cover absent or malformed metadata, missing or empty resource scopes, and empty, throwing, or unsupported resource-session lookup, against open and gated indexes. Successful resource-token use, interactive consent, transient authentication failures, and sign-out races remain covered.

## Validation

- `node build\npm\electronTypes.ts && npm run typecheck-client` - passed.
- `npm run valid-layers-check` - passed.
- `npm run precommit` - passed; both changed files checked.
- `node build\next\build-fast.ts --client-only` - passed; generated client output in this worktree.
- `$env:VSCODE_SKIP_PRELAUNCH = '1'; & .\scripts\test.bat --run src\vs\workbench\services\extensionManagement\test\electron-browser\extensionGalleryManifestService.test.ts --timeout 20000 --reporter dot` - passed; 76 tests.

Scenarios.Scenario: Cold startup with a configured Microsoft marketplace
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The eager manifest service waits sequentially for sign-in session lookup, entitlement parsing, protected-resource metadata discovery, optional resource-scoped session lookup, and the marketplace manifest GET. Shared-process and remote-server publication runs from the completion callback and is not required for getExtensionGalleryManifest() to return.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Resolve Microsoft sign-in sessions through IAuthenticationService.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One sign-in-session lookup per account resolution.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same sign-in-session lookup occurred before the diff.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Must finish before metadata or manifest retrieval begins.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Fetch RFC 9728 protected-resource metadata through IRequestService.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One successful request, or up to two serialized well-known requests for a service URL with a path when the first candidate fails.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same discovery ran for every eligible Microsoft account resolution.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Must finish before choosing a marketplace bearer and before the manifest GET.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Resolve a resource-scoped Microsoft authentication session.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One lookup when valid metadata advertises at least one scope; zero when scopes are empty.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Previously one lookup also ran for empty scopes by substituting configured sign-in scopes; the diff removes that call. Non-empty scopes still perform one lookup.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: When performed, it blocks the subsequent manifest GET.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Fetch and parse the configured marketplace manifest.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One request per completed account resolution, with no retry in this path.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same single manifest request occurred, but missing metadata or resource-session failure could attach the sign-in bearer; the diff makes those requests anonymous without adding another request.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: This is the final network operation required to make the manifest available.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Publish manifest, token, and service URL to the shared process and optional remote server.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One shared-process call and at most one remote-server call per published manifest update.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same channel fan-out existed; the diff only changes token content in affected branches.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Calls are launched after manifest resolution and are not awaited by getExtensionGalleryManifest().

Scenarios.ScalingInput: A single configured marketplace and selected account; multiplicity is bounded to one resolution pipeline, not extension count or catalog size.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Concurrent callers of getExtensionGalleryManifest() share extensionGalleryManifestPromise. Within one resolution, authentication and network boundaries are serialized. The diff does not increase concurrency; empty-scope metadata now removes one authentication lookup.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: The initial manifest promise coalesces cold concurrent callers and remains warm thereafter. Protected-resource discovery has no result or negative cache in this provider, while the last valid protectedResource is retained for interactive sign-in. The diff does not alter those lifecycles; it only suppresses resource-session lookup for an advertised empty scope list.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the sequential call path, request cardinality, coalescing promise, and changed empty-scope branch are explicit in code and regression tests.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Authentication-provider and network latency vary by deployment, but the diff does not add any boundary on this path and removes one lookup for empty scopes.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression. Missing metadata and unavailable resource sessions change only which bearer is attached; request count and serialization are unchanged. Empty scopes perform less critical-path authentication work than before.

Scenarios.CriticalPath: Each Microsoft session-change event invokes handleMarketplaceAccountAccess, which resolves the account and repeats metadata/authentication work before issuing the manifest GET; only the latest generation may publish a result.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: React to a Microsoft session event and query sign-in/resource sessions.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One sign-in lookup, plus at most one resource lookup, per event; empty-scope metadata now yields zero resource lookups.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same event-driven resolution existed, and empty scopes previously caused an additional resource-session lookup.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: These operations must finish before the winning refresh can request the manifest, although superseded operations may still complete.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One successful or up to two failed serialized metadata requests per session event.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Same per-event discovery and cancellation behavior before the diff.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Blocks each event's account resolution; superseded metadata requests are not canceled.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Fetch the marketplace manifest for a non-superseded eligible resolution.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: At most one manifest request per resolution that reaches this stage; later events cancel earlier manifest requests.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Same request and cancellation structure; only bearer selection changes.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Required before the refreshed catalog is published.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Authentication session event frequency, normally low and unrelated to extension catalog size.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: beginResolution cancels the previous resolution token and supersedes earlier results. Authentication and metadata discovery do not receive that token, so rapid events can overlap those pre-manifest operations, but that behavior is pre-existing and the diff neither raises event frequency nor adds work.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Account-event refreshes bypass the initial coalescing promise and metadata discovery is uncached. The retained protectedResource assists sign-in but does not cache event refresh discovery. These behaviors are unchanged by the diff.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High for the pre-existing event and cancellation flow; high that the diff only removes an empty-scope resource lookup.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Bursty provider events could expose pre-existing overlapping metadata work, but no changed line increases frequency, cardinality, or lifetime.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression. The changed branches preserve or reduce boundary cardinality and do not amplify the pre-existing uncanceled metadata work.

Scenarios.Scenario: Interactive Microsoft sign-in or consent after access is required
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The user action waits for account enumeration/selection, sign-in session creation, optional metadata discovery, silent resource-session lookup, and optional resource consent creation.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Enumerate accounts and create the sign-in authentication session.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One account enumeration and one sign-in session creation per user action.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Interactive and required before any resource consent attempt.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Discover marketplace protected-resource metadata when no valid resource was retained.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Zero when protectedResource is retained; otherwise one successful or up to two failed serialized requests per sign-in action.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: When needed, blocks completion before consent handling.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Silently query a resource session, then interactively create one when absent.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: For non-empty scopes, one lookup and at most one creation. For empty scopes, both are now skipped.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Empty scopes previously fell back to sign-in scopes and could perform both authentication calls; the diff removes them. Non-empty advertised scopes preserve prior cardinality.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: These calls delay completion of sign-in when present.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: One selected account and one marketplace per explicit user action.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: The operations are awaited sequentially for one chosen account. No batching or parallel fan-out is present. The changed empty-scope branch returns before both resource authentication operations.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: A previously discovered valid protectedResource is reused for sign-in. Missing or malformed metadata is not negatively cached, so a later user action can rediscover it; that behavior is unchanged. Resource-session caching is owned by the authentication provider.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the guards and sequential awaits are explicit, and tests assert zero resource requests for missing or empty scopes.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Provider UI and consent duration vary, but the only performance-relevant changed branch eliminates calls.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression. The diff shortens the empty-scope path and does not add work to non-empty consent.

Analysis.Summary: Completed the performance pass over both changed files and all diff pages. Traced cold startup, session-change refresh, and interactive sign-in through authentication, network discovery, manifest fetch, cache/coalescing, cancellation, and IPC publication. The production changes either preserve boundary counts while withholding an invalid fallback bearer or remove authentication calls for empty scopes; no actionable performance regression was introduced.
